subject: System Design
title: The Flash Crash of 2010
description: A 60-second lesson on The Flash Crash of 2010.

hook.text: On May 6, 2010, the US stock market dropped 1,000 points in 5 minutes and recovered 10 minutes later.

buildup.text: A single trader placed a massive automated sell order using an algorithm, triggering panic.

discovery.text: High-frequency trading algorithms detected the sell pressure and amplified it by selling even faster.

twist.text: Some stocks briefly traded for $0.01. Others jumped to $100,000. Market prices became meaningless.

climax.text: Automated systems without circuit breakers created a feedback loop that nearly collapsed the market.

punchline.text: Algorithms panicking caused a trillion-dollar flash crash.

quiz.question: What amplified the 2010 Flash Crash?
options: High-frequency trading algorithms created a feedback loop
A power outage at the exchange
